_meta.indication: TYKERB is indicated in combination with capecitabine for the treatment of patients with advanced or metastatic breast cancer whose tumors overexpress HER2 and who have received prior therapy including an anthracycline, a taxane, and trastuzumab.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multicenter trial comparing lapatinib plus capecitabine versus capecitabine alone; enrollment was stopped early based on a pre-specified interim analysis.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with HER2 (ErbB2) over-expressing (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ confirmed by FISH) locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer progressing after prior anthracyclines, taxanes, and trastuzumab.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to progression (TTP), defined as time from randomization to tumor progression or death related to breast cancer.
pivotal_trials.n: 399 patients enrolled (198 lapatinib plus capecitabine; 201 capecitabine).
pivotal_trials.result: By independent assessment, median TTP 27.1 weeks vs 18.6 weeks; Hazard Ratio 0.57 (95% CI 0.43, 0.77); p value 0.00013.

key_safety: Most common (>20%) adverse reactions were diarrhea, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, nausea, rash, vomiting, and fatigue. Diarrhea occurred in 65% (Grade 3 13%) vs 40% with capecitabine alone. Decreases in LVEF and QT prolongation were observed.
target_moa: Lapatinib is a 4-anilinoquinoxaline kinase inhibitor of the intracellular tyrosine kinase domains of both EGFR (ErbB1) and HER-2 (ErbB2) receptors, inhibiting ErbB-driven tumor cell growth.

description.text: Added use in combination with letrozole for postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer (accelerated approval)

citations.quote: This supplemental new drug application provides for the use of Tykerb® (lapatinib) tablets in combination with letrozole tablets for the treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive metastatic breast cancer that overexpresses the HER2 receptor for whom hormonal therapy is indicated. Tykerb® in combination with an aromatase inhibitor has not been compared to a trastuzumab-containing chemotherapy regimen for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to regular (full) approval based on study LAP016A2307

basis.text: The application received Priority review designation.

summary.text: Lapatinib received Fast Track designation and Priority review, and was granted regular (full) approval based on the single randomized study EGF100151.

citations.quote: Fast Track Designation: lapatinib received Fast Track designation on 28 October 2003 for the treatment of patients with refractory advanced or metastatic breast cancer who have ErbB2 overexpression

This reviewer recommends a regular approval for this NDA. The recommendation is based on the efficacy and safety results of a single study, EGF 100151, which is a randomized, open label trial comparing the lapatinib and capecitabine combination to capecitabine alone in patients with advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

requirement.text: Perform an in vivo drug interaction study of the ability of steady-state lapatinib dosing to alter the pharmacokinetics of a single dose of midazolam (CYP3A4 inhibition).

citations.quote: Based upon the ability of lapatinib to act as a CYP 3A4 inhibitor in vitro, GSK agrees to perform an in vivo drug interaction study of the ability of steady-state lapatinib dosing to alter the pharmacokinetics of a single dose of midazolam.
